title: Hybrid SLO-adaptive throttler with KV slab compaction and cooperative preemption windows
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Recent regressions under mixed-tenant workloads show tail-latency SLO violations when large KV-resident contexts cause GPU memory pressure. Current preemption is blunt: we evict entire KV segments or hard-kill queued microbatches which introduces quality and throughput cliffs. We need a throttling and preemption strategy that preserves latency SLOs for high-priority tenants while minimizing throughput and quality impact for others, and which cooperates with the GPU slab allocator and KV cache residency logic.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 99th percentile token latency for P0 tenants stays within configured SLO (e.g., +10ms of baseline) under mixed load (10% noisy tenants). 2) Overall throughput drop < 8% compared to baseline steady-state. 3) KV hit-rate degradation for background tenants < 12% on average. 4) No OOMs observed during 6h soak in staging with synthetic hotset. 5) End-to-end experiment documented with dashboard links and A/B comparison.
implementation_notes: Plan: implement a hybrid controller that combines token-budget annealing, per-tenant cooperative preemption windows, and slab-aware KV compaction hints.
decisions: Use a two-tier budget: immediate-latency-budget (short horizon) + compaction-budget (medium horizon) so tenants can borrow soft tokens within limits.
Cooperative preemption: workers will advertise microbatch 'yield points' so long-running batches can be split at cache-safe boundaries rather than being force-aborted.
KV slab compaction: integrate with GPU slab allocator to compact cold KV slabs during low-util windows and prefer compaction over eviction for slabs that free contiguous memory.
Graceful demotion: when forced, background tenants get degraded model variants (quantized or shorter context) as fallback before eviction.
Expose three new config knobs to Console: priority-weight, borrow-window-ms, compaction-threshold-percent.
No changes to client API; routing logic remains backward compatible.
timeline: Week 1: prototype controller + metrics. Week 2: integrate with slab allocator and KV compaction hooks. Week 3: staging soak + perf runs. Week 4: refine heuristics and roll to canary.
